findings.summary: Relative imports use `.ts` extensions (env.ts, schema.ts); under NodeNext+verbatimModuleSyntax tsc -b fails with TS5097 and the whole apps/api typecheck breaks.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite line 5 to `from '../shared/env.js'` and line 6 to `from './schema.js'` — matches the project convention set by shared/logger.ts and modules/auth/tokens.ts. Re-run `pnpm --filter @medbridge/api typecheck` to confirm zero errors.

findings.summary: Module top-level `pool = new Pool(...)` plus `export const db = createDb(pool)` opens a real pg connection pool at import time and re-imports the eager env singleton already flagged in wave-3 F-001 — defeats the buildApp(env) DI seam.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the eager singletons: export only `createDb(pool)` and a `createPool(env: Env)` factory. main.ts (wave-7) builds them once after loadEnv(); integration tests inject their own Pool. Same posture as the wave-3 F-001 / F-002 logger fix.

findings.summary: hashRefreshToken returns `string` synchronously, but the task spec mandates `Promise<string>`; callers typed against the spec will hit a TS signature mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Either change the signature to `async function hashRefreshToken(raw: string): Promise<string>` (return the digest directly — async wraps it) or escalate to the planner for a spec amendment. Sync is fine at runtime; the issue is the contracted Promise return type.

findings.summary: Pool sizing (max 10, idleTimeoutMillis, connectionTimeoutMillis) is hardcoded; the task spec said `sized from env` but env.ts has no DB_POOL_MAX/timeouts. Builder hit a planner gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) extend env.ts with DB_POOL_MAX / DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS / DB_CONN_TIMEOUT_MS (note env.ts is not in this task's target_files — planner must amend) and read them here, or (b) accept the constants and amend the task spec. Surface this to the planner via step.ask before wave-5.

findings.summary: tokens.ts calls loadEnv() at module top-level for the fail-fast side-effect, but the eager `export const env = loadEnv()` in shared/env.ts already validates at first import; the second call is redundant.
findings.suggested_fix: Once wave-3 F-001 lands (eager singleton removed), tokens.ts' explicit loadEnv() call becomes the canonical fail-fast trigger. Until then, leave a JSDoc comment noting the redundancy and rely on env.ts's singleton.

findings.summary: Barrel intentionally empty per task spec (downstream tasks add module schemas). Matches ARCHITECTURE.md §4.2.
findings.suggested_fix: No action this wave. When wave-5+ adds modules/*/schema.ts, re-export here.
